prompt: On sorted distinct input, first-element-pivot quicksort is much slower than random-pivot quicksort on average. Why?

options.text: The fixed pivot repeatedly removes only the smallest remaining value.
options.explanation: That creates unbalanced partitions; uniform pivots remove this systematic input-order effect in expectation.

options.text: Random pivots guarantee perfectly balanced partitions.
options.explanation: Individual random choices can still be poor.

options.text: The random version skips sorting some elements.
options.explanation: Both must produce the full correct ordering.

options.text: Sorted input changes the comparison rules.
options.explanation: The work difference comes from partition shape, not a different ordering relation.

workedExample: Trace the first-element version: each partition leaves almost the entire array to recurse on. Random ranks give a better expected partition pattern, but unlucky runs and duplicate keys still need attention in real implementations.
